items.title: Codemod reports errors but still exits successfully
items.recommendation: Set `process.exitCode = 1` or throw when `totalErrors > 0`, and avoid printing the success message in that path. If partial rewrites are possible, make the summary explicitly distinguish applied changes from failed files.
items.reproduction: Run `anvil-codemod imports` against an input that makes `rewriteImportsInFile` return at least one error; the CLI prints the error count but completes without setting `process.exitCode`, so the shell observes success.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this CLI command, and the package scripts only define build/codemod commands rather than assertions about exit status.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CLI-level test that stubs or triggers a transform error, runs the `imports` command, and asserts a non-zero exit code plus no 'Changes applied successfully' message.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `tools/codemods/src/cli.ts` error summary handling and add a focused CLI exit-status test.

items.title: DiagnosticLocation omits documented null line and column values
items.recommendation: Change the nullable location fields to include null, for example line?: number | null, column?: number | null, end_line?: number | null, and end_column?: number | null, or update the contract text if null is no longer valid on the wire.
items.reproduction: const loc: DiagnosticLocation = { file: 'README.md', line: null }; // TypeScript rejects null under strictNullChecks
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The diagnostics test only covers the omitted-field case and asserts line/column are undefined after JSON round-trip. It never constructs or type-checks an explicit null location value.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a diagnostics type parity test that constructs a Diagnostic with location: { file: 'README.md', line: null, column: null } and round-trips it through JSON, if null is valid per the wire contract.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/diagnostics/types.ts plus the diagnostics parity test

items.title: Package bin can no-op when invoked through a symlinked binary
items.recommendation: Use a more robust main-module check for Node ESM, for example compare realpath-normalised file paths for import.meta.url and process.argv[1], or remove the guard from the actual bin entrypoint and keep import-safe behaviour in a separate module.
items.reproduction: Install/link the package so node_modules/.bin/anvil-admin points at apps/admin-cli/dist/index.js, then execute node_modules/.bin/anvil-admin --help. If process.argv[1] is the bin link while import.meta.url is the resolved dist file URL, the guard is false and run() is never called.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing run() test calls run() directly with argv values; it does not execute the packaged bin path or exercise the invokedAsBin guard.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that imports or executes the built entrypoint through a symlinked bin path and asserts --help exits 0 with help output, or factor the main detection into a helper and cover symlink-normalised paths.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/admin-cli/src/index.ts main-entry guard plus a focused test in apps/admin-cli/src/__tests__/index.test.ts

items.title: Shell integration tests source the wrapper path without shell quoting
items.recommendation: Add a small shell-quoting helper for paths embedded in `bash -c` scripts, or avoid string interpolation by passing the script path as an argument/environment variable and sourcing `"$ANVIL_RUN_SCRIPT"`. Apply it consistently at all three call sites.
items.reproduction: Run the crate tests from a checkout path containing a space, or adjust the test to source a copied `anvil-run.sh` from a temp directory named with a space; the generated `. /path/with space/anvil-run.sh` command will not source the intended file.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests use the current `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, which usually has no whitespace or shell metacharacters, so the unquoted path bug is not exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Copy `shell/anvil-run.sh` into a temp directory whose name contains a space, source that copied path through the same test helper, and assert the dispatcher still invokes the stub.
items.minimumFixScope: Change `crates/anvil-run/tests/shell_integration.rs` to quote or otherwise safely pass `script_path()` in all generated bash snippets.

items.title: In-flight connects can resurrect or duplicate live transports
items.recommendation: Track an in-flight connect promise/generation and make connect() return that promise while state is connecting or reconnecting. In openTransport(), after await transport.connect(), check that the attempt generation is still current and state is not closed before assigning this.transport; otherwise close the just-opened transport and return or throw an anvil-driver-closed error. close() should invalidate pending connection attempts so late completions cannot publish a transport.
items.reproduction: Use a transportFactory whose connect() returns a manually resolved promise. Call const p = client.connect(); then await client.close(); then resolve the transport connect promise and await p. The current implementation ends with state effectively connected and a live transport installed after close. Similarly, Promise.all([client.connect(), client.connect()]) before either connect resolves constructs two transports.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: driver-client.test.ts covers sequential connect idempotence after connection is already established and close() after a completed connect, but it has no delayed transport test for concurrent connect() calls or close() while connect() is in flight.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fake transport recipe with a deferred connect promise. Assert that two concurrent connect() calls create only one transport, and assert that close() before resolving the deferred connect leaves the client closed, closes the late transport, and makes subsequent request() reject with anvil-driver-closed.
items.minimumFixScope: DriverClient connection lifecycle state in packages/anvil-driver-client/src/client/driver-client.ts plus targeted unit tests in packages/anvil-driver-client/src/client/driver-client.test.ts.

items.title: Standalone daemon command is not covered by process-level tests
items.recommendation: Add a small process-level integration test for the binary contract, at minimum covering help/usage and invalid invocation. If feasible on Unix, also spawn `anvil-intercept start` under an isolated temporary HOME/state directory, send SIGTERM, and assert it exits successfully.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Both included test files construct `IpcListener` or service harnesses in-process, bypassing `crates/anvil-intercept/src/main.rs` entirely.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Use `CARGO_BIN_EXE_anvil-intercept` or an `assert_cmd` equivalent to verify `anvil-intercept --help`, `anvil-intercept` without a subcommand, and a Unix-only `anvil-intercept start` smoke test that terminates via SIGTERM in a temporary environment.
items.minimumFixScope: Add binary-level integration coverage for `crates/anvil-intercept/src/main.rs`; no daemon library changes are required.

items.title: Malformed JSON-RPC responses are classified as valid responses
items.recommendation: Validate the full response shape before returning kind: 'response': id must be string, number, or null; success responses must have result and no error; error responses must have error as a non-null object with numeric code and string message; responses with both result and error should be rejected as unknown or surfaced as a protocol error.
items.reproduction: Call classifyIncoming({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 'req-1', error: 'boom' }); it returns kind: 'response'. If the caller then handles it as JsonRpcErrorResponse, errorFromResponse receives a string error value and reads response.error.message/code as undefined.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current classifyIncoming tests cover valid success/error responses and a few non-response shapes, but they do not include malformed error objects, invalid ids, or result/error mutual-exclusion cases.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add classifyIncoming tests asserting kind === 'unknown' for { jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 'req-1', error: 'boom' }, { jsonrpc: '2.0', id: {}, result: true }, and { jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 'req-1', result: true, error: { code: -32603, message: 'x' } }.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/framing/jsonrpc.ts plus jsonrpc.test.ts

items.title: Same-key requests stop coalescing once the debounce timer fires
items.recommendation: Track active in-flight dispatch state per key in addition to timer-pending state. When a later submit supersedes the same key, mark the earlier active generation stale and settle its public promise as `coalesced` or ignore its eventual dispatcher result so it cannot seed the cache or return stale diagnostics.
items.reproduction: Use an injected scheduler with debounceMs=0 and a dispatcher whose promise is manually deferred. Submit key `file:///x` with content A, advance the scheduler so dispatch A starts but does not resolve, then submit the same key with content B and advance again. Both dispatch functions are invoked and both returned promises can resolve as `fresh` instead of the earlier one being coalesced or suppressed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing coalescing tests only submit replacements before the debounce timer fires and assert `dispatchCount` is still zero before the final advance. They never hold a dispatcher unresolved after the timer has fired and then submit a same-key replacement.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a `MidEditDebouncer` test where the first same-key dispatch starts and remains unresolved, a second same-key submit occurs, and the assertions prove only the current generation can produce a `fresh` result or seed the dedup cache.
items.minimumFixScope: `packages/anvil-driver-client/src/midedit/debouncer.ts` plus focused tests in `packages/anvil-driver-client/src/midedit/debouncer.test.ts`; add a `validateMidEdit` regression only if the public envelope semantics change.

items.title: Expired dedup entries for inactive keys are retained indefinitely

evidence.symbol: cache expires after the dedup window

items.recommendation: Prune expired cache entries opportunistically on submit, add a bounded cache size, or schedule expiry cleanup using the injected scheduler. Keep cleanup deterministic under fake schedulers so tests can verify it.
items.reproduction: Submit successful requests for many distinct keys, advance the scheduler past `dedupWindowMs`, and do not submit those keys again. The entries remain in `dedupCache` until `clearDedupCache()` or process teardown.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current expiry test advances past the window and re-submits the same key, which exercises the only implemented delete path. It does not create multiple inactive keys or assert that stale entries for untouched keys are removed.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test-only cache size accessor or observable pruning hook, submit several unique keys, advance beyond the dedup window, trigger cleanup with a different key, and assert expired inactive keys no longer remain cached.
items.minimumFixScope: `packages/anvil-driver-client/src/midedit/debouncer.ts` and `packages/anvil-driver-client/src/midedit/debouncer.test.ts`.

items.title: CLI build can fail because importHelpers is enabled without a tslib runtime dependency
items.recommendation: Either remove importHelpers from the admin-cli tsconfig, or add tslib as a production dependency for @eddacraft/admin-cli.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise source files through Vitest/tsx-style TypeScript execution, not the compiled dist package installed with only production dependencies.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package smoke test that runs the built dist/index.js from a production-install style environment, or a manifest check asserting tslib is present whenever importHelpers is enabled.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/admin-cli/tsconfig.json or apps/admin-cli/package.json

items.title: scan_buffer spoof-block invariants are not encoded in the public type
items.recommendation: Model the result as a union that separates the diagnostic response from the spoof-block response, and make `AnvilScanBufferSpoofBlock.reason` the literal type `'degraded:spoofed-attribution'`. Export the spoof-block type through the same barrel if it is part of the public protocol surface.
items.reproduction: A TS consumer can currently type-check an invalid result such as `{ version: 1, diagnostics: [diag], truncated: false, spoof_block: { reason: 'typo', fenced_worktree: '/tmp/wt' } } satisfies AnvilScanBufferResult`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The protocol test only constructs the non-spoof diagnostic result and checks `truncated`; it never constructs a valid spoof-block result or asserts that invalid spoof-block combinations fail type-checking.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add typecheck-backed cases for a valid spoof-block response plus `// @ts-expect-error` cases for a non-literal reason and for combining spoof_block with diagnostics.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protocol/types.ts and the protocol barrel/tests if the spoof-block type is public.

items.title: parseAgentTag accepts inherited fields as required wire keys
items.recommendation: Treat AgentTag envelopes as plain JSON records: reject arrays, and require Object.hasOwn(obj, 'driver_id'), Object.hasOwn(obj, 'claimed_agent_id'), and Object.hasOwn(obj, 'pid_starttime') before reading the values. Preserve dropping unknown own fields for forward compatibility.
items.reproduction: Object.assign(Object.prototype,{driver_id:'anvil-run',claimed_agent_id:'forged',pid_starttime:1}); try { parseAgentTag({}) } finally { delete Object.prototype.driver_id; delete Object.prototype.claimed_agent_id; delete Object.prototype.pid_starttime; } returns a tag instead of throwing.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The session tests check null, primitive, missing-field, and numeric validation cases, but no test supplies inherited required properties or a prototype-polluted object. The array test only passes because Array.prototype is clean in that test process.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a hostile-input test where required fields exist only on the prototype and assert parseAgentTag throws for the first missing own field; optionally also assert arrays are rejected before field lookup.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/session/types.ts and packages/anvil-driver-client/src/session/types.test.ts

items.title: Pending backpressure sends resolve successfully when the connection closes
items.recommendation: Track both resolve and reject for pending writes. On drain, resolve pending writes; on close/error before drain, reject them with `anvil-daemon-transport-drop`. Consider resolving via the write callback on successful flush instead of a separate resolve-only drain queue.
items.reproduction: Use a slow or paused daemon connection so socket.write() returns false, call send(), then close the peer before drain. The pending send promise resolves from fireClose() rather than rejecting with a transport-drop error.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing transport tests send a tiny message and wait for a normal echo, so socket.write() is expected to return true. They do not simulate backpressure, peer drop during a pending write, or assertion of send promise outcome under close.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test with a paused server or mocked net.Socket where write() returns false and no drain fires before close/error; assert the pending send() rejects with `anvil-daemon-transport-drop`.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the writePromises storage and close/error handling in both UnixSocketTransport and WindowsNamedPipeTransport; add shared backpressure regression tests.

items.title: Windows named-pipe transport does not verify current-user ownership
items.recommendation: Implement a real Windows ownership gate before resolving connect(): derive the current user SID and require the canonical suffix to match it, and inspect the named pipe security descriptor/ACL via a native helper or other trusted boundary. If that cannot ship yet, make Windows named-pipe connection unsupported rather than accepting same-prefix pipes as owner-validated.
items.reproduction: Create or point DriverClientOptions.pipeName at a user-controlled pipe named \\.\pipe\anvil-intercept-S-1-5-21-anything. validateWindowsPipeName accepts it as long as the suffix has no whitespace or slashes, and connect() proceeds without proving ownership.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/transport/windows.test.ts only exercises string-shape validation and explicitly avoids opening or inspecting any pipe, so it cannot catch ACL or current-SID bypasses.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Windows-only test or native-helper-backed unit test that rejects a same-prefix pipe whose suffix is not the current user SID or whose ACL grants another user access, and accepts only the daemon's current-user-owned pipe.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/transport/windows.ts plus Windows transport tests; possibly add a small native/PowerShell ACL inspection helper if pure Node cannot read the pipe security descriptor.

items.title: Peer/error close does not put transports into the closed state before later sends
items.recommendation: In fireClose(), set `this.closed = true` and `this.socket = null` before invoking handlers and before draining any waiters. Ensure subsequent send() calls always reject with `anvil-daemon-transport-drop` after any close cause.
items.reproduction: Connect to a server that accepts and then closes the socket. After the transport's onClose('peer') fires, call transport.send('x'). The send path does not hit the closed guard because fireClose() left closed false and socket non-null.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The Unix happy-path test only calls send before close and asserts that some close event fired. There is no test that calls send after peer close or error close. The Windows tests do not exercise transport lifecycle at all.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add lifecycle tests for both concrete transports (or a shared fake socket harness) that trigger peer close/error, wait for onClose, then assert send() rejects with DriverClientError code `anvil-daemon-transport-drop` without waiting for drain.
items.minimumFixScope: Update fireClose() in packages/anvil-driver-client/src/transport/unix.ts and packages/anvil-driver-client/src/transport/windows.ts, then add lifecycle regression coverage.

items.title: Successful responses can be treated as success when the body read fails
items.recommendation: Do not swallow response.text() failures. Catch them separately and throw an AdminError with an appropriate non-success exit code, status, and a message that preserves the read failure cause.
items.reproduction: Use a fetchImpl that returns a Response-like object with status 200 and text() rejecting. Calling client.get('/x') without a schema resolves to undefined instead of throwing an AdminError.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: apps/admin-cli/src/__tests__/client.test.ts covers network fetch rejection, 4xx/5xx bodies, invalid JSON, empty schema responses, and schema validation, but it does not cover response.text() rejection after fetch has resolved.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a client test with a fetchImpl returning an object whose status is 200 and whose text() rejects, then assert client.get('/x') rejects with AdminError instead of resolving undefined.
items.minimumFixScope: Update AdminClient.request body-read handling and add one focused regression test in apps/admin-cli/src/__tests__/client.test.ts.

items.title: Parsers accept inherited fields as trusted wire data
items.recommendation: Read required fields through an own-property helper, for example check Object.hasOwn(obj, key) before accessing obj[key], and apply it consistently for ProtectionClaim and SurfaceClaim fields. Keep unknown extra own fields ignored for forward compatibility.
items.reproduction: const polluted = Object.create({ schema_version: 'anvil.protection-claim.v1', worktree_state: 'full', surfaces: [] }); parseProtectionClaim(polluted) returns a valid claim instead of rejecting the envelope as missing required own fields.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The hostile-input test only covers JSON.parse('{"__proto__": ...}'), where __proto__ is an own data property and required fields are not inherited. It does not cover objects whose prototype actually contains the required fields, nor global prototype pollution.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that parseProtectionClaim(Object.create({ schema_version: PROTECTION_CLAIM_SCHEMA_VERSION, worktree_state: 'full', surfaces: [] })) and parseSurfaceClaim(Object.create({ identifier: 'mcp', state: 'participating' })) both throw missing-field TypeErrors.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protection_claim/types.ts plus protection_claim parser hostile-input tests

items.title: Air-gapped status verification can still attempt network refresh before running the local probe
items.recommendation: Special-case local/offline status verification before silent refresh, or add an auth-check mode that refuses/returns auth-required without refresh for commands documented as air-gapped. Then run the air-gapped harness without `ANVIL_DEV` against an isolated expired credential fixture with a refresh token.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included air-gapped test bypasses auth with `ANVIL_DEV=1`, so it verifies the status command body but not the global auth layer that runs first in production.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend `air_gapped.rs` with a test that seeds isolated expired credentials containing a refresh token, runs `anvil --no-tui --json status --verify` through the network-blocked harness without `ANVIL_DEV`, and asserts the process does not attempt or hang on network refresh.
items.minimumFixScope: `crates/anvil-cli/src/main.rs` auth pre-dispatch policy for documented local/offline commands plus the air-gapped credential fixture test.

items.title: Pre-dispatch JSON auth responses are written to stderr despite successful exit
items.recommendation: When `auth_required_response` returns an informational EXIT_OK JSON envelope, print it to stdout. Keep true error envelopes on stderr if that is the project convention, but do not put successful JSON-mode output solely on stderr.
items.reproduction: Run a gated action command with no credentials, for example with an empty XDG_CONFIG_HOME: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$(mktemp -d) anvil --json status`. The process exits 0, stdout is empty, and the JSON authRequired envelope is on stderr.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The main.rs unit tests assert the returned envelope shape and exit code but never exercise process stdout/stderr routing. The included JSON integration tests cover stdout parsing for doctor, edda, gate, and status --verify; none covers a gated action command stopped by pre-dispatch auth.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that runs `anvil --json status` or another gated action command with isolated empty credentials, asserts exit code 0, asserts stdout parses as `{ "state": "authRequired", ... }`, and asserts stderr does not contain the only JSON payload.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the pre-dispatch auth-required print path in crates/anvil-cli/src/main.rs and add one CLI integration test for the JSON stdout contract.

items.title: JSON-mode auth failures emit human text before the JSON error envelope
items.recommendation: Thread JSON/machine-output mode into auth evaluation, or make `check_auth` return a structured auth error without printing when `global.json` is set, leaving `main` as the single JSON error renderer.
items.reproduction: env -u ANVIL_DEV -u ANVIL_LICENSE ANVIL_NO_PROMPT=1 XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$(mktemp -d) cargo run -p eddacraft-anvil -- --json status 2>err; cat err
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included JSON-mode tests either use unauthenticated commands or set `ANVIL_DEV=1`, so they never exercise the gated auth-failure path in JSON mode.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that runs a gated command such as `anvil --json status` with isolated empty credentials and `ANVIL_NO_PROMPT=1`, then asserts stderr is exactly one parseable JSON object and contains no human auth guidance.
items.minimumFixScope: `crates/anvil-cli/src/main.rs` auth error rendering plus one auth-failure JSON integration test.

items.title: Malformed JSON-RPC error responses can throw through the transport callback
items.recommendation: Validate response envelopes before classifying them as JsonRpcResponse, or harden handleResponse/errorFromResponse to reject malformed response payloads with an `anvil-daemon-invalid-request`/framing error event without throwing. Require error.code to be a number and error.message to be a string before treating it as a JSON-RPC error response.
items.reproduction: Connect a DriverClient with a fake transport, issue request('session.list'), then push an inbound line `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"req-1","error":null}\n`. The pending request is deleted and errorFromResponse throws while handling the inbound frame.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The JSON-RPC tests cover valid success/error responses and a few unknown frames, but they do not include malformed response-shaped frames where `error` is null, a primitive, or missing required fields.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a jsonrpc/client test that sends `{ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 'req-1', error: null }` for an in-flight request and asserts the client does not throw synchronously; it should settle the request with a structured error or emit a non-fatal error event.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/framing/jsonrpc.ts and the corresponding jsonrpc/driver-client tests.

items.title: Concurrent connect calls can open and leak multiple transports
items.recommendation: Track an in-flight connect promise and return it when state is 'connecting' or 'reconnecting', or otherwise serialise connect attempts. Ensure a failed in-flight connect clears the stored promise and a successful one leaves exactly one owned transport.
items.reproduction: Use a transportFactory whose connect() promise is externally controlled. Call `const a = client.connect(); const b = client.connect();` before resolving either connect promise. The factory is invoked twice and two transports can become connected, but only the last assignment is closed by client.close().
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current connect idempotency test awaits the first connect before calling the second, so it never exercises the 'connecting' state race.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a DriverClient test with a deferred fake transport connect; invoke connect() twice concurrently, resolve the deferred connect, assert the factory was called once and both promises resolve, then close and assert the one transport closed.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/client/driver-client.ts and packages/anvil-driver-client/src/client/driver-client.test.ts.

items.title: Benchmark reports can be overwritten by runs started in the same second
items.recommendation: Make report paths collision-resistant and non-clobbering, for example by including subsecond time plus process id or a UUID, and create the file with exclusive-create semantics so collisions fail instead of overwriting.
items.reproduction: Start two `cargo run -p anvil-bench --release -- graph_memory` processes from the same directory within the same Unix second; both compute the same `bench-results/stress-<timestamp>.json` output path and one report is lost.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests exercise the CLI entrypoint or concurrent/same-second output path generation; existing report serialization tests do not validate collision behaviour for main.rs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration-style test around output path generation or a refactored `run` helper that forces the same timestamp for two runs and asserts the second run does not overwrite the first report.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the output filename/open mode in `crates/anvil-bench/src/main.rs`; factor path generation into a small testable helper if needed.

items.title: Root tsconfig lists files that TypeScript does not actually check
items.recommendation: Either remove the inert entries and keep this as a narrow TypeScript-only config check, or add a dedicated config-check tsconfig that enables `allowJs`/`checkJs` for eslint.config.mjs and uses the current E2E path, likely `apps/e2e/**/*` if root-level E2E files are still intended.
items.reproduction: `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit --explainFiles | rg 'eslint\.config|jest\.config|e2e|vitest\.config|playwright\.config'` only reports vitest.config.ts and playwright.config.ts as matched by tsconfig.json.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this config. The existing root TypeScript invocation succeeds because TypeScript silently ignores the unmatched or unsupported include entries.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small validation script or test that runs `tsc --explainFiles` for the root config and asserts every intentional include entry is either matched or explicitly documented as inert.
items.minimumFixScope: Update tsconfig.json include entries and, if JS config checking is intended, the compilerOptions needed to make eslint.config.mjs part of the checked program.

items.title: Root Vitest discovery can miss package __tests__ directories outside src
items.recommendation: Add an include pattern for package __tests__ directories that are not necessarily under src, or align the documented convention and config so there is a single discoverable test location. Consider disabling passWithNoTests at the root config if CI expects the root suite to find tests.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or config smoke tests are included that assert the Vitest include globs discover expected repository test locations.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small config-level test or CI smoke check that uses Vitest's resolved config/glob matching to assert packages/example/__tests__/sample.test.ts and packages/example/src/sample.test.ts are both discoverable.
items.minimumFixScope: vitest.config.ts include globs and, if retained intentionally, an explicit documented rationale for passWithNoTests.

items.title: Node type definitions exceed the supported runtime contract
items.recommendation: Either align @types/node to the minimum supported Node major, or raise the engines.node minimum if Node 25 APIs are intentionally allowed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests exercise adapter parsing and serialization behavior; they do not verify package metadata consistency or run the suite against the minimum supported Node runtime.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package metadata validation test that checks the @types/node major does not exceed the minimum engines.node major, or add CI coverage on Node 22 that catches runtime use of newer Node APIs.
items.minimumFixScope: package.json devDependency or engines.node

items.title: Release package root and manifest entrypoints disagree
items.recommendation: Choose one package shape and make the release config match it: either publish from the project root with files pointing at dist, or generate/copy a dist/package.json whose main/types/exports point at ./index.js and other dist-relative files.
items.reproduction: Build the package and publish or pack from packages/adapters/dist as configured by nx-release-publish; the package root will not contain files at ./dist/index.js relative to that root.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included Vitest suites exercise source imports and adapter behaviour, but there is no packaging smoke test that builds and resolves the package from the configured release packageRoot.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a packaging test that runs the adapters build, verifies packages/adapters/dist/package.json exists with dist-relative entrypoints, then imports the packed package entrypoint with Node.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/package.json and packages/adapters/project.json, plus the build/release step that creates the published manifest.

items.title: Documented subpath imports are blocked by package exports
items.recommendation: Add explicit subpath exports with both import and types targets for the supported public barrels, or change the README to require root imports only. Also correct the SpecKit example to use an actually exported symbol, such as SpecKitFormatAdapter or createSpecKitAdapter.
items.reproduction: Install or link the package with its current exports map, then run `node -e "import('@eddacraft/anvil-adapters/bmad')"`; Node will reject the subpath because it is not present in package.json exports.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests import implementation files with relative paths under src, so they never exercise Node package exports or the README's public import examples.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-resolution test that builds the library and dynamically imports the documented root, speckit, bmad, generic, and utility entrypoints through the package name.

Either make bmadToAPS return a structured object containing plan, errors, and warnings, or throw when conversion errors are present so BMADFormatAdapter.parse returns createParseError. Non-fatal omissions should at least be returned as warnings.

items.title: Vercel ignore command path arguments are shell-parsed without validation
items.recommendation: Validate `rootDirectory` and every `extraWatchPaths` entry with a conservative path allowlist, or centralise shell argument rendering with correct POSIX single-quote escaping and use it for all dynamic arguments.

items.title: License verification accepts tokens without an expiry
items.recommendation: After jwtVerify, require payload.exp to be a finite number, or pass requiredClaims: ['exp'] if supported by the jose version in use. Consider also requiring issuer/audience if BAuth has a stable token contract.

items.title: Array undefined values make object hashing throw instead of producing a stable JSON-equivalent hash
items.recommendation: Handle undefined array elements explicitly, most likely by serializing them as null to match JSON.stringify array semantics, or document and validate that undefined is forbidden anywhere inside arrays.

items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a canonicalizeJSON test asserting canonicalizeJSON([1, undefined, 3]) is '[1,null,3]' and, if sparse arrays are supported, canonicalizeJSON([, 2]) is '[null,2]'.

items.title: SpecKit format serialize/reparse loses change paths
items.recommendation: Make serialization and parsing agree on the path contract. For example, emit backticked paths in headings or a `Path: \`...\`` line, and add parser support for the serialized heading format.

The parsed change description is 'Create src/auth/controller.ts', but its path becomes src/generated-file.ts instead of src/auth/controller.ts.

items.title: SpecKit input limit counts UTF-16 code units instead of bytes
items.recommendation: Use Buffer.byteLength(content, 'utf8') for the SpecKit size guard, matching the generic parser behaviour.
items.reproduction: Call new SpecKitParser().parseSpecMarkdown('😀'.repeat(Math.floor((2 * 1024 * 1024) / 4) + 1)); the UTF-8 byte length is over 2 MiB while string.length is below MAX_INPUT_SIZE, so the size guard does not throw.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test covers parseGeneric only; no included SpecKitParser test asserts byte-length enforcement for multibyte content.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a SpecKitParser parseSpecMarkdown test mirroring the generic multibyte case and expecting /maximum size/ when UTF-8 bytes exceed MAX_INPUT_SIZE.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the guard in packages/adapters/src/speckit/parser.ts and add a focused parser test.

items.title: Empty-change exports produce NaN task progress
items.recommendation: Handle the zero-task case explicitly, for example by reporting 0% progress when tasks.length is 0 or omitting the progress percentage for empty task lists.
items.reproduction: Call SpecKitExportAdapter.convertFromAPS with a valid APS plan whose proposed_changes is []. The conversion succeeds and the returned tasksContent contains `Progress: NaN%`.

items.title: require-cwd-restoration accepts a restore before the cwd-changing call
items.recommendation: Track the sequence of chdir calls and only count a saved-cwd chdir as restoration for a preceding non-restoration chdir, or require the saved-cwd chdir to occur after a cwd-changing call in the same relevant scope.

items.title: Public template mutations can desynchronise the explain service
items.recommendation: Keep the service state tied to the registry. Options include not exporting clearTemplates from the public explain index, making clearTemplates reset the service flag through a single owner, or having ensureTemplatesInitialised verify required built-in templates before returning.
items.reproduction: Call initExplainService(); clearTemplates(); then isExplainable('ARCH-001') or explainByRule('ARCH-001'). The service does not re-register built-in templates because templatesInitialised is still true.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Tests reset through resetExplainService() or test template-loader in isolation; none compose public clearTemplates/registerTemplate with the high-level explain-service APIs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a public-API test that initialises the service, calls clearTemplates(), and verifies the next explainByRule('ARCH-001') either reinitialises built-ins or that clearTemplates is no longer exported for consumers.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/explain/index.ts and/or packages/anvil/core/src/explain/explain-service.ts, with one explain-service integration test.

items.title: similarWarnings can become negative when the current warning is not in allWarnings
items.recommendation: Clamp the value at zero or only subtract when the current warning is actually present in the same-rule/same-file set.
items.reproduction: Call explainWarning with an ARCH-001 warning and allWarnings set to [] or to warnings from other files only. The returned boundary explanation has related.similarWarnings === -1.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing similar-count test only covers the happy path where allWarnings includes the current warning and another same-file warning; it does not cover an empty or partial allWarnings list.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that calls explainWarning(archWarning, []) and asserts related.similarWarnings is 0 or undefined, never negative.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/explain/explain-service.ts buildContext plus a focused explain-service regression test.

items.title: Exported API composition has only CORS preflight coverage
items.recommendation: Add a small index-level integration test that imports ../index.js and asserts representative mounted routes under /api/v1, including /health and at least one route behind the global middleware stack.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests mount route modules such as auth and admin on fresh Hono instances, so they prove route-local behaviour but not the exported app's base path, route registration, or middleware ordering. cors.test imports index.ts but only covers one waitlist preflight.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: In apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__/index.test.ts, mock db/licence dependencies as needed, import ../index.js, and assert /api/v1/health responds with the expected shape plus representative /api/v1/auth/verify and /api/v1/admin/invite requests reach the mounted route/middleware rather than returning 404.
items.minimumFixScope: Test-only change under apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__ for exported app composition.

items.title: Queued waiters can be bypassed by new direct acquisitions
items.recommendation: Before direct acquisition, check the queue for existing entries from other agents. If the queue is non-empty, join it and only acquire when this agent is first. Alternatively make direct acquisition conditional on an empty queue under the same queue-file lock.
items.reproduction: Have A hold a lock, have B call `waitForLock` and enter the queue, release A's lock, then have C call `waitForLock` before B's next poll. C can acquire directly without joining behind B.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The queue tests cover position ordering after explicit `join` calls, but they do not cover `waitForLock` with an existing waiter and a later contender.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a `waitForLock` fairness test where an existing queued agent must acquire before a newcomer when the lock becomes available.
items.minimumFixScope: QueueManager.waitForLock acquisition ordering and corresponding fairness tests.

items.title: Concurrency subpath is advertised but not exported
items.recommendation: Add a `./concurrency` export with `types` and `import` entries pointing at `./dist/concurrency/index.d.ts` and `./dist/concurrency/index.js`, and verify the build emits that directory.
items.reproduction: Install or build the package as an ESM dependency, then run `node -e "import('@eddacraft/anvil-runtime/concurrency')"`; Node will reject the unexported subpath.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The listed tests import concurrency files by relative source paths and do not exercise package-level exports or the generated hook import path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package export smoke test that builds the runtime package and dynamically imports `@eddacraft/anvil-runtime/concurrency` through the package exports map.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/package.json plus any build/package export smoke test needed to verify the subpath.

items.title: Agent registry updates can lose concurrent registrations and heartbeats
items.recommendation: Protect all registry mutations with a registry file lock or switch to per-agent registry records so independent agents do not overwrite a shared JSON object.
items.reproduction: Start two AgentManager instances with different agent IDs and call `register()` concurrently against an empty registry. Both can read an empty registry and save a single-agent registry; the final file may contain only one agent.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No listed AgentManager tests exercise concurrent registration, heartbeat, unregister, or stale cleanup against the same registry file.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a concurrent registration test that launches multiple AgentManager.register calls and asserts the final registry contains every agent with correct heartbeat metadata.
items.minimumFixScope: AgentManager registry mutation methods and concurrent registry tests.

items.title: Queue mutations are only partially serialised
items.recommendation: Use the same per-queue file lock for every queue mutation, including leave, getStatus cleanup, cleanupAllTimedOut, and waitForLock's leave-on-acquire/timeout paths.
items.reproduction: Run one agent leaving a queue while another joins the same resource. If both read the old queue before either final write, whichever writes last determines the file and can drop the other update.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The queue tests are sequential and do not create concurrent join/leave or cleanup interleavings.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add concurrent join/leave tests that assert no joined entry is dropped and no leaving entry is resurrected after both operations complete.
items.minimumFixScope: QueueManager mutation methods and queue concurrency tests.

items.title: Expired or stale lock takeover is not mutually exclusive
items.recommendation: Serialize all lock state transitions, including renewals and force-acquire, behind the same per-lock sentinel or implement a compare-and-swap check that only succeeds when the existing lock still matches the lock that was read.
items.reproduction: Create an expired lock, then start two LockManager instances with different agent IDs and call `acquire({ type, resource })` concurrently. Both can observe the expired file before either write completes and both can receive `acquired: true`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing expired-lock test performs a single sequential takeover; it does not race two contenders against the same expired or stale lock.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a concurrent expired-lock takeover test that releases a barrier after both contenders have observed the expired lock and asserts exactly one acquisition succeeds.
items.minimumFixScope: LockManager takeover and renewal paths, plus concurrency tests for expired/stale takeover.

items.title: Requirements sections are parsed twice because both header patterns match the same heading
items.recommendation: Make the patterns mutually exclusive, remove the duplicate generic Requirements pattern, or collect sections/items into a Set before returning them.
items.reproduction:
parseGeneric('# Plan

## Requirements
- Add login
- Add logout
') will produce four requirement-derived changes instead of two because extractRequirements reads the same section once per matching pattern.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: parser.test.ts only checks input size limits and does not assert parsed requirements or proposed_changes counts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parseGeneric test with a single '## Requirements' section containing two list items and assert exactly two proposed_changes are produced.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/generic/utils.ts extractRequirements

items.title: Numbered requirements parse successfully but fail generic detection and validation scoring
items.recommendation: Count numbered markdown list items in analyzeContent using the same list grammar supported by the parser, and include them in listItemCount/hasLists.
items.reproduction:
A document such as '# Plan

## Requirements
1. Add login
2. Add logout
3. Add reset password
' has parseable requirements, but analyzeContent reports hasLists=false and listItemCount=0, leaving confidence below the 30% validation threshold for typical short documents.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests do not exercise detect(), validate(), or numbered-list parsing behavior.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add adapter detect/validate tests for a numbered-only Requirements section and assert detection succeeds and validation has no LOW_CONFIDENCE error.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/generic/utils.ts analyzeContent list detection

items.title: Parsed generic plans receive a hash computed over the placeholder hash field
items.recommendation: Build a planWithoutHash object in genericToAPS or parse(), compute generateHash(planWithoutHash), and return { ...planWithoutHash, hash }. Avoid including any placeholder hash in the hashed payload.
items.reproduction: Parse any generic markdown document through GenericMarkdownAdapter.parse, then validate the returned APS plan with hash validation enabled. The calculated hash over the plan content without the hash field will differ from the stored hash generated at packages/adapters/src/generic/format-adapter.ts:88.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included parser tests only exercise the byte-size guard, and serializer tests do not call GenericMarkdownAdapter.parse or validate generated hashes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a GenericMarkdownAdapter.parse test that parses a representative markdown document and asserts the returned hash equals generateHash({ ...plan, hash omitted }).
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/generic/parser.ts and packages/adapters/src/generic/format-adapter.ts hash construction path

items.title: README says every traversal attempt throws, but exists intentionally returns false
items.recommendation: Adjust the README API contract to state that exists() returns false for blocked or inaccessible paths, while mutating and reading operations throw on traversal or symlink escape.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover the intended exists() behavior; they do not validate README/API text against that exception.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/shared/storage/README.md to document the exists() exception.

items.title: Dangling final symlink can escape the storage sandbox on write
items.recommendation: In the ENOENT path, lstat the requested final path before treating it as a new file and reject if it is a symlink, or use no-follow/openat-style file creation where available. Keep the existing parent realpath walk for missing intermediate paths, but also validate the final path object when it exists as a dangling symlink.
items.reproduction: Create base and outside directories. Inside base, create a symlink named link pointing to outside/new.txt, where new.txt does not exist but outside exists. Then call await storage.write('link', 'escaped'). The current resolvePath path returns base/link and fs.writeFile follows the symlink, creating outside/new.txt.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The symlink write test covers a symlink to an existing outside file, where realpathSync succeeds and the current code rejects. There is no test for a final-component symlink whose outside target is missing.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a non-Windows test that creates symlinkSync(join(outsideDir, 'new.txt'), join(tempDir, 'dangling-write-link')), calls storage.write('dangling-write-link', 'data'), expects a path escape error, and asserts outsideDir/new.txt was not created.
items.minimumFixScope: Update FileStorage.resolvePath's ENOENT handling for final-component symlinks and add the focused regression test in file-storage.test.ts.

items.title: Bundle downloads can follow redirects to non-HTTPS hosts with credentials
items.recommendation: Resolve redirects against the original URL, reject non-HTTPS redirects except explicit localhost test cases, cap redirect depth, and strip Authorization and other sensitive headers when the redirect changes origin.
items.reproduction: Configure an https bundle URL with bearer auth that responds 302 Location: http://attacker.example/bundle.tar.gz. The recursive download sends the Authorization header to the redirected HTTP URL.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The redirect test intentionally exercises an HTTP localhost redirect and only asserts success; it does not cover HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade, cross-origin redirects, or credential preservation across redirects.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests for an HTTPS-origin redirect to HTTP non-localhost expecting failure, and for cross-origin HTTPS redirects expecting Authorization not to be forwarded.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/policy/src/bundle-manager.ts redirect handling and BundleManager redirect/auth tests.

items.title: Ed25519 is advertised as supported but cannot verify with Node crypto
items.recommendation: Implement Ed25519 using crypto.verify(null, Buffer.from(data), publicKey, signature), or remove Ed25519 from the supported/default algorithms until it is implemented and tested.
items.reproduction: Generate an Ed25519 key pair, sign the canonical files array with crypto.sign(null, data, privateKey), configure BundleVerifier with algorithm Ed25519, and verifyBundle(); the Ed25519 case throws during createVerify and the result is unverified.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The crypto verification tests cover RS256 and ES256 only; there is no Ed25519 positive-path test despite Ed25519 being in DEFAULT_ALLOWED_ALGORITHMS.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a valid Ed25519 signed bundle test that expects verifyBundle() to return verified=true and keyId for the Ed25519 key.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/policy/src/bundle-verifier.ts Ed25519 branch and BundleVerifier Ed25519 tests.

items.title: Bundle signature verification accepts unsigned files in the bundle
items.recommendation: During verification, enumerate all policy/data files that are allowed to be part of the signed bundle, require every relevant file to appear exactly once in the verified manifest, and reject empty file lists or unexpected extra files.
items.reproduction: Create policy.rego, sign a manifest listing only policy.rego, then add evil.rego beside it. verifyBundle() still returns verified=true because evil.rego is never compared against the manifest.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests cover valid manifests with one or more listed files and tampering of a listed file, but they never add an extra unlisted bundle file or use an empty signed file list.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a BundleVerifier test that signs only policy.rego, writes an additional unsigned extra.rego, and expects verifyBundle() to fail with an unsigned/uncovered file error.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/policy/src/bundle-verifier.ts plus focused BundleVerifier tests.

items.title: Failed bundle updates delete the last valid cached bundle
items.recommendation: Extract updates into a separate temporary directory, fully validate extraction and signatures/checksums there, then atomically replace the old bundle directory only after the new bundle is ready. On failure, leave the existing cache entry and files untouched.
items.reproduction: Download a valid bundle with a short refresh interval, wait for expiry, then have the server return a corrupt gzip/tar. The second download fails and the original bundle directory has been removed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover cache reuse, checksum failure before deletion, invalidation, and cache clearing, but not an expired cached bundle where extraction of the replacement fails after the old directory is removed.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that seeds a cached bundle, forces it expired, serves an invalid tarball, asserts downloadBundle() fails, and asserts getBundle() still returns the original path with policy.rego present.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/policy/src/bundle-manager.ts extraction/replace flow and one cache-preservation regression test.

items.title: BundleManager signature_key contract is unusable for signed bundle downloads
items.recommendation: Define the signature source explicitly. Either integrate BundleVerifier/.signatures.json after extraction, or add config for a signature URL/path, download/read it deliberately, and resolve signature_key file paths before calling crypto.verify.
items.reproduction: Configure a bundle with signature_key set to a valid public key file path. downloadBundle() looks for <cache>/<name>.tar.gz.tmp.sig, then passes the path string as the key material, so verification fails.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: BundleManager tests disable signature verification in the shared setup and only cover checksum validation, so no test exercises signature_key, key-file paths, or sidecar signature retrieval.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add BundleManager tests for inline PEM and key-file signature verification using a generated signed tarball/signature pair, including a missing signature case with a clear error.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/policy/src/bundle-manager.ts signature handling and BundleManager signature tests.

items.title: Human input IDs are returned but never emitted
items.recommendation: Add the generated identifier to the human_input observation contract and emitted payload, or stop generating/returning a link ID if human_input observations are intentionally unaddressable.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this source group, and the feature metadata lists an empty tests array.

items.title: queryMemories does not apply pagination defaults for raw query objects
items.recommendation: Parse or normalise incoming queries at the MemoryStore boundary before filtering, including defaulting include_superseded, limit, offset, sort_by, and sort_order consistently.
items.reproduction: After saving at least one memory, call store.queryMemories({} as MemoryQuery). The result page is empty because the computed end index is NaN instead of defaulting to offset 0 and limit 100.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The MemoryStore tests use the local queryDefaults helper, so they never call queryMemories with omitted pagination fields even though the public query schema supports defaulted pagination.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a MemoryStore test that saves a memory and asserts queryMemories({} as MemoryQuery) returns it with limit 100, offset 0, and has_more computed from those defaults.
items.minimumFixScope: Normalise query defaults in MemoryStore.queryMemories and add a focused test for an empty query object.

items.title: Promotion validation can throw TypeError instead of returning schema errors
items.recommendation: Use the safeParse result as the source for field-level checks, or guard with typeof input.reason === 'string' and typeof input.promoted_by === 'string' before trimming.
items.reproduction: Call validatePromotionInput with a payload that is missing reason or promoted_by, cast as PromoteProposalInput. Instead of returning validation errors, it throws when accessing .trim() on undefined.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current Zod schema violation test removes proposal_id, leaving the fields used by the extra trim checks intact.
