items.title: Search misses matches beyond the index preview
items.recommendation: Either store a separate full searchable statement in the index, or when query.search is present, load candidate memories and apply the search predicate to memory.statement rather than the truncated index preview.
items.reproduction: Save a memory whose statement is 120+ characters and contains a unique token only after the first 100 characters, then call searchMemories with that token. The memory will not be returned because queryMemories filters against the truncated index statement.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The search test uses 'Use deterministic plan checks in CI.', where the searched token appears inside the first 100 characters, so the index preview and full statement behave the same.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a MemoryStore test that saves a memory with a long statement containing a unique token after character 100 and asserts searchMemories(token) returns that memory.
items.minimumFixScope: Update MemoryStore search filtering and add a regression test in packages/edda-stack/src/edda/memory-store.test.ts.

items.title: Typecheck target combines `--noEmit` with `emitDeclarationOnly`
items.recommendation: Remove `emitDeclarationOnly` from the docs-shell tsconfig used for application typechecking, or split declaration-emitting settings into a separate build tsconfig that is not used by the `tsc --noEmit` target.
items.reproduction: Run `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/docs-shell typecheck` or the Nx `docs-shell:typecheck` target with this tsconfig.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included Vitest suites exercise runtime helpers only; they do not invoke the package or Nx typecheck target.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CI/package validation check that runs the docs-shell typecheck target, or ensure the existing workspace typecheck includes this project.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `apps/docs-shell/tsconfig.json` or the docs-shell typecheck/build target configuration so no target passes `--noEmit` while loading a config with `emitDeclarationOnly`.

items.title: Refresh rotation consumes the old token before new credentials are durably issued
items.recommendation: Make refresh rotation atomic at the database boundary where possible: consume the old token and insert the replacement in one transaction, and avoid exposing the client to a consumed-old/no-new-token state. At minimum, add explicit recovery semantics for post-consume failures so retries do not trigger family theft detection for server-side issuance failures.
items.reproduction: Simulate consumeRefreshToken resolving true and insertRefreshToken or signLicence throwing during POST /auth/session/refresh. The old token is already consumed, no new raw refresh token reaches the client, and a retry with the old token will be treated as token reuse.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The auth-session tests cover happy path, invalid tokens, consumed-token reuse, and concurrent consume failure. They do not cover downstream failures after consumeRefreshToken succeeds, such as insertRefreshToken or signLicence throwing.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test where consumeRefreshToken succeeds but insertRefreshToken rejects, asserting the implementation does not leave the old token consumed without a retry-safe outcome; add a similar test for licence signing failure after replacement creation.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/routes/auth-session.ts and the refresh-token query/transaction helper used by that route.

items.title: Default invite flow advertises requested scopes but never persists them for activation
items.recommendation: Persist the granted scopes in the default invite transaction, matching /admin/approve's access_tokens insert pattern, or change the API to reject scoped default invites if only tokenOnly/approve can establish scoped grants.
items.reproduction: POST /admin/invite with {"email":"alice@example.com","scopes":["preview","beta"]} and tokenOnly omitted/false, then complete the device activation flow. The invite response reports preview+beta, but no access_tokens row was created for those scopes, so /auth/device/poll cannot issue a licence with the preview grant.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included default invite test only uses the implicit ['beta'] default and asserts the response shape. It does not send non-default scopes or assert that the transaction includes an INSERT INTO access_tokens for the default device-code invite path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an admin invite test for tokenOnly=false with scopes ['preview','beta'] that asserts the transaction includes an access_tokens insert containing those scopes, then add/extend a device activation test to assert the issued licence preserves the preview scope for that invite path.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/routes/admin.ts default /admin/invite transaction and the corresponding admin/device route tests.

items.title: OTP active-code limit is enforced with a check-then-insert race
items.recommendation: Move the cap enforcement into a single database operation, for example an INSERT ... SELECT guarded by a COUNT predicate in a transaction/serializable block, or a per-user partial constraint/lock that prevents more than the configured number of active unconsumed, unexpired codes.
items.reproduction: Send several POST /auth/otp/request calls concurrently for the same active user when they have fewer than three active codes. Each request can read the same pre-insert count and then insert its own OTP row, resulting in more than MAX_ACTIVE_CODES active rows.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test sets countActiveOtpCodes to 3 and verifies a single request does not insert. It does not exercise concurrent requests where the count is below the limit for every racing caller.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a query-level or integration test that fires concurrent OTP requests with the active count initially below MAX_ACTIVE_CODES and asserts the database ends with no more than three active codes for the user.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/routes/auth-otp.ts plus the OTP insert/count query helper so the limit is enforced atomically.

items.title: Packaged API omits the migration CLI and migration inputs it advertises
items.recommendation: Either include the migration CLI and SQL migration files in the package artefact, or change the migration command to use packaged dist assets and ensure the build copies migrations there. If migrations are source-checkout-only by design, do not advertise the command in a package manifest used for release artefacts.
items.reproduction: Run npm pack or pnpm pack for apps/anvil-api and inspect the tarball: package.json will contain the migrate scripts, but scripts/migrate.mjs and src/db/migrations are not included because package.json files only allows dist and README.md.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests exercise the source implementation imported from ../db/migrate.js with temporary fixture directories. They do not exercise package packing, package.json files filtering, or the scripts/migrate.mjs wrapper's resolved paths.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package/artefact smoke test that builds apps/anvil-api, creates the packed artefact or packlist, and asserts that the migration entrypoint plus the SQL migration directory used by that entrypoint are present and addressable.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/package.json files/build scripts plus apps/anvil-api/scripts/migrate.mjs pathing if migrations are copied to dist

items.title: Plan-based filters receive relative paths while planless filters receive absolute paths
items.recommendation: Compute the absolute fullPath before applying filter in the plan-based branch, and call filter(fullPath) there just as normaliseTargetFiles does.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this source group, and the owned file contains no co-located assertions covering filter parity between planless and plan-based contexts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a runtime test that passes the same workspace-relative file through context.targetFiles and context.plan.proposed_changes with a filter asserting path.isAbsolute(input), and verify both modes return the same absolute path.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/types/gate.types.ts plan-based branch in getFilesFromContext, plus a focused unit test for filter callback path shape parity.

items.title: E2E package imports undeclared direct dependencies
items.recommendation: Add all directly imported packages to apps/e2e/package.json, using workspace:* for workspace packages and the appropriate dependency/devDependency entry for jose.
items.reproduction: Run the e2e package in an isolated or strict pnpm install without root/transitive hoisting; the direct jose, @eddacraft/anvil-contracts, or @eddacraft/anvil-api imports are not guaranteed to resolve from apps/e2e.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests execute inside the current workspace layout, where aliases or hoisting can mask missing manifest edges. There is no manifest-dependency validation for direct imports.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a dependency hygiene check such as knip/depcheck or a package graph rule that fails when apps/e2e imports undeclared external or workspace packages.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/e2e/package.json and the lockfile if dependency metadata changes require it

items.title: Status filters are dropped from generated context bundles
items.recommendation: Add `statuses?: Array<'open' | 'locked' | 'completed' | 'cancelled'>` to `ContextBundleJSON.filter` and populate it from `criteria.statuses` in `buildContextBundleJSON`. Consider including it in the Markdown bundle's filtered-by line as well for parity.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests check that scopes and tags are preserved in the JSON bundle, but there is no test for `criteria.statuses` in either JSON or Markdown context bundle output.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a context bundle test that filters with `{ statuses: ['locked'] }` and asserts `bundle.filter.statuses` equals `['locked']`.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/aps/src/filter/context-bundle.ts plus the associated filter tests.

items.title: Parser accepts governance tables that are not immediately after the H1
items.recommendation: Change table discovery to validate the immediate top-level sequence after the H1: metadata table first, relationships table next, allowing only non-semantic whitespace because blank lines are not AST nodes. Reject any intervening non-table content before either required table.
items.reproduction:
Call parseDocGovernance on markdown shaped like `# Title

Intro prose before metadata.

| Type | Authority | Owner | Status | Freshness |
| ---- | --------- | ----- | ------ | --------- |
| Guide | Authoritative | x | Live | 2026-01-01 |

| Upstream | Downstream |
| -------- | ---------- |
| a | b |`. It returns parsed metadata instead of rejecting the misplaced tables.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover the happy path and cases where a required table is entirely absent, but they do not include valid-looking tables preceded by prose or another block after the H1.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test asserting ParseError when a paragraph or heading appears between the H1 and the metadata table, and another asserting ParseError when prose appears between the metadata and relationships tables.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/docs-meta/src/parser/parse-metadata.ts and packages/docs-meta/src/parser/parse-metadata.test.ts

items.title: rule panic isolation is not valid in release builds with panic=abort
items.recommendation: Either build the daemon/rule-execution path with panic="unwind" if catch_unwind is the intended boundary, or move rule execution behind a process boundary so aborting rules cannot terminate the daemon. Add the documented multi-process release fixture before treating the contract as covered.
items.reproduction: Run the daemon in a release profile configured with panic="abort" and install a rule equivalent to panicking_rule_service; sending rule_panic_request aborts the daemon process instead of returning the unwind-mode empty diagnostics response.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current Rust fixture explicitly pins only panic="unwind" behaviour under cargo test and documents the panic="abort" release path as an unimplemented follow-up.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a multi-process release-profile test that starts the daemon with a panicking rule and asserts the expected release contract, either no daemon abort or a controlled child-process failure with daemon survival.
items.minimumFixScope: Release profile or rule-execution isolation strategy, plus the midedit_contract release-mode regression fixture.

items.title: stale PID recovery can remove a newly-created live PID file
items.recommendation: Serialise PID-file recovery and daemon ownership with an actual lock, or make recovery remove only the exact file identity that was inspected. On Unix, hold a lock file or locked open PID file across recovery and daemon lifetime; do not rely on a read/status/remove/create sequence alone.
items.reproduction: Start two run_foreground instances concurrently against the same stale PID file, with recovery interleaved so both read the stale record before either remove_file call completes. The second remover can unlink the first starter's replacement PID file.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover stale recovery and that Drop preserves an already-replaced PID file, but they do not run two stale-recovery attempts concurrently or force the interleaving between stale read, first recreate, and second remove.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Unix test that uses two coordinated tasks/processes and an injected recovery hook to pause both after stale-status detection, then lets one recreate the PID file before the other attempts removal. Assert the live replacement is not removed and only one daemon proceeds.
items.minimumFixScope: PidFileGuard acquisition and stale PID recovery logic in crates/anvil-intercept/src/lib.rs, plus a targeted concurrent stale-recovery regression test.

items.title: Exported package version is stale relative to the manifest
items.recommendation: Derive PACKAGE_VERSION from the release source of truth during build, or update the constant whenever package.json is bumped. Add a metadata regression test so release bumps cannot drift silently.
items.reproduction: Build or import the package root and compare PACKAGE_VERSION with packages/edda-stack/package.json version; the exported value is 0.1.0 while the manifest is 0.6.2-beta.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests exercise config and contract modules directly through ./config.js or ./contracts/*.js imports. None of the included tests imports packages/edda-stack/src/index.ts or asserts that PACKAGE_VERSION matches the package manifest.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a root index metadata test that imports PACKAGE_VERSION and reads packages/edda-stack/package.json, then expects PACKAGE_VERSION to equal the manifest version.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/edda-stack/src/index.ts metadata handling and add a package-root metadata test.

items.title: Package test script can pass with zero contract tests
items.recommendation: Add focused schema tests for accepted and rejected response shapes, and make the package test command fail when no tests are discovered, for example by adding an explicit local Vitest include for `src/**/*.test.ts` and disabling pass-with-no-tests behaviour.
items.reproduction: Run `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/admin-contracts test`; it exits 0 and reports `No test files found, exiting with code 0`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no linked tests, and the package's current `vitest run` invocation reports zero discovered test files while still succeeding.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add `packages/shared/admin-contracts/src/index.test.ts` covering representative valid and invalid parses for each exported response schema, especially `SendMigrationResponseSchema`, timestamp coercion, nullable timestamps, and ID coercion.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the admin-contracts package test setup and add schema tests under `packages/shared/admin-contracts/src`.

items.title: Common registry is not covered by the linked registry tests
items.recommendation: Add a focused test file for packages/adapters/src/common/registry.ts that imports from ../../common or ../common as appropriate and covers duplicate registration, unregister/clear behavior, getAdapterForFormat, listSupportedFormats, and detectFormat.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current linked tests target packages/adapters/src/base/registry.ts through a relative import from packages/adapters/src/base/__tests__, so they do not instantiate or assert the common AdapterRegistry implementation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create packages/adapters/src/common/__tests__/registry.test.ts with a mock SpecToolAdapter and assertions for register, duplicate register error, unregister, getAdapterForFormat, listSupportedFormats, clear, and detectFormat.
items.minimumFixScope: Add direct unit coverage for packages/adapters/src/common/registry.ts and include it in the existing packages/adapters vitest run.

items.title: Published architecture template loader loses its YAML templates
items.recommendation: Make template assets part of the build output, for example by copying `src/architecture/templates/*.yaml` to `dist/architecture/templates` during build/pack, or embed the template data in TypeScript so no runtime file asset is required.
items.reproduction: Run the package build, then execute the built `dist/architecture/templates/index.js` API and call `getTemplate('layered')`; it attempts to read `dist/architecture/templates/layered.yaml`, which the `tsc` build does not emit.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The template tests run against the source tree where the YAML files exist beside `src/architecture/templates/index.ts`; they do not exercise the built or packed package layout.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a post-build/package-layout test that imports the built architecture template module from `dist` and calls `getTemplate` for every built-in template.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the core package build/packaging path for architecture template YAML assets and add a built-output smoke test.

items.title: Architecture baseline inference follows symlinked directories out of the workspace
items.recommendation: Use `lstatSync` to skip symlinked entries by default, or resolve realpaths and enforce that descendants remain inside `workspaceRoot` while tracking visited directories to avoid cycles.
items.reproduction: Create a workspace containing a symlinked directory such as `src/outside -> /some/large/tree` or `src/loop -> ..`, then call `inferBaseline(workspaceRoot)`. The walker follows the symlink because `statSync` reports the target directory.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The analyzer tests cover normal filtering and missing/unreadable paths, but they do not create symlinked directories or cyclic directory structures for `inferBaseline`.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an `inferBaseline` test with a symlinked directory pointing outside the temp workspace and assert the collected module count excludes files behind the symlink.
items.minimumFixScope: Harden `collectSourceFiles` in `packages/anvil/core/src/architecture/analyzer.ts` and add symlink traversal coverage.

items.title: Documented .anvil compiler API is not reachable from package consumers
items.recommendation: Either add an `./anvil-format` entry to `package.json` exports and keep its declarations in dist, or re-export the anvil-format barrel from `src/index.ts` if it is intended to be part of the root API. If it is intentionally internal, update the README so it does not describe the compiler as active package surface.
items.reproduction: Install or pack the package, then try `import { compilePatterns } from '@eddacraft/anvil-core/anvil-format'`; Node will reject the unexported subpath. Trying the root import also fails because `src/index.ts` does not re-export the symbol.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The compiler tests import `compilePatterns` via `./compile.js`, so they validate implementation behaviour but not package-level importability through `package.json` exports or the root barrel.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package API smoke test that imports `@eddacraft/anvil-core/anvil-format` from the built package output and asserts `compilePatterns` is exported.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `packages/anvil/core/package.json` exports and/or `packages/anvil/core/src/index.ts`, plus one public API smoke test.

items.title: Generated dependency-cruiser config is CommonJS despite using a .js filename
items.recommendation: Emit a `.cjs` config filename for CommonJS output, or generate ESM syntax when the target workspace is ESM. Keep the consumer command/config path in sync with the chosen extension.
items.reproduction: Use `compileArchitecture` in a project with `package.json` containing `"type":"module"`, then load the generated `.anvil/dependency-cruiser.js` with Node/dependency-cruiser. The file is parsed as ESM but contains CommonJS assignment.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The dc-generator tests parse the returned string to inspect JSON rule content; they do not execute or load the generated config under an ESM package boundary.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that creates a temp workspace with `package.json` set to `type: module`, runs `writeDCConfig`, and verifies the generated file can be loaded by the intended dependency-cruiser loading path.
items.minimumFixScope: Change `DC_CONFIG_FILENAME`/generated module syntax and update tests around generated config loadability.

items.title: Targeting rules can reference variants that do not exist
items.recommendation: In FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema.check, build the set of variant keys and validate every targeting rule's variant against it, emitting an issue at ['targeting', ruleIndex, 'variant'] when it is unknown.
items.reproduction: FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema.safeParse(validFlag({ targeting: [{ conditions: [{ attribute: 'environment', operator: 'equals', value: 'prod' }], variant: 'missing' }] })) currently succeeds even though 'missing' is not in variants.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover defaultVariant reference validation and valid targeting rules, but there is no negative test for a targeting rule whose variant is absent from variants.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema with targeting test that uses variant: 'nonexistent' and expects safeParse(...).success to be false.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/contracts/src/schemas/feature-flags.schema.ts plus the feature flag schema tests.

items.title: Structured debug payloads bypass redaction
items.recommendation: Sanitise structured payloads before passing them to `console.debug`. A minimal fix is to serialize unknown objects through a safe redacting replacer or recursively clone primitives/arrays/plain objects while applying `sanitizeForLog` to string values and known secret-bearing keys.
items.reproduction: Set `ANVIL_DEBUG=1`, call `createDebugger('api')('request', { authorization: 'Bearer abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz012345' })`, and observe that `console.debug` receives the unredacted object as its second argument.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests do not include `debug.ts`, and no test spies on `console.debug` with object payloads while debug logging is enabled.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a `debug.test.ts` case that enables `ANVIL_DEBUG`, logs an object containing a Bearer token and API-key-like value, and asserts the `console.debug` arguments contain `[REDACTED]` and not the original secret.
items.minimumFixScope: `apps/anvil-api/src/lib/debug.ts` plus focused unit coverage for string, Error, and object payload redaction.

items.title: Licence verification returns malformed claims as `LicenceClaims`
items.recommendation: Validate every claim that is returned through the `LicenceClaims` interface: `identity` must be an object with `provider: string` and `id: string | null`, `org` must be `string | null` when present, `tier` must be a string, `scopes` must be an array of strings, and `seats` should be a finite positive integer if present. Return `null` for malformed signed payloads.
items.reproduction: Sign a JWT with the configured test private key containing `email: 'a@b.com'`, `scopes: [123]`, and `identity: 'bad'`, plus the correct issuer/audience/expiry. `verifyLicence` will return a non-null object instead of rejecting the malformed claims.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The licence tests cover missing `scopes`, but they do not cover malformed claim types inside otherwise valid signed JWTs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend `licence.test.ts` with signed JWTs that have `scopes: [123]`, `identity: 'github'`, and `seats: '1'`, and assert `verifyLicence` returns `null` for each malformed payload.
items.minimumFixScope: `apps/anvil-api/src/lib/licence.ts` claim validation and targeted `verifyLicence` regression tests.

items.title: Top-level rustdoc incorrectly says the 80-writer stress test is ignored
items.recommendation: Update the `crates/anvil-witness/src/lib.rs` deferred follow-up text to match the current test state, or remove the deferred follow-up entirely if MLP2-015 completed it.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests exercise writer concurrency behaviour, but they do not validate rustdoc accuracy or cross-document consistency.
items.minimumFixScope: Edit the stale crate-level documentation in `crates/anvil-witness/src/lib.rs`.

items.title: BMAD serializer emits unknown metadata values as document text
items.recommendation: Read BMAD metadata through narrow helpers, e.g. use typeof value === 'string' && value.length > 0 before interpolation, otherwise fall back to docs/PRD.md and Project.
items.reproduction: Serialize an APS plan with metadata: { outputFile: { path: 'docs/PRD.md' }, projectName: 123 }. The BMAD output contains output_file: "{project-root}/[object Object]" and '# 123 - Product Requirements Document'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked serializer type-safety tests cover serializeToGeneric only. There are no corresponding BMAD serializer tests for non-string outputFile or projectName metadata.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add BMAD serializer tests that pass non-string outputFile and projectName metadata and assert the output falls back to docs/PRD.md and Project rather than stringifying the values.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/bmad/serializer.ts plus BMAD serializer metadata type-safety tests.

items.title: BMAD input size guard counts UTF-16 units instead of bytes
items.recommendation: Use Buffer.byteLength(content, 'utf8') for the BMAD size check, matching the generic parser guard.
items.reproduction: Call parseBMADDocument('\u{1F600}'.repeat(Math.floor((2 * 1024 * 1024) / 4) + 1)). Buffer.byteLength exceeds 2 MiB, but content.length remains under the current limit, so the maximum-size error is not thrown.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked byte-length regression tests target parseGeneric only. There is no equivalent BMAD test for multi-byte input at the 2 MiB boundary.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a BMAD parser test mirroring packages/adapters/src/generic/__tests__/parser.test.ts that asserts parseBMADDocument rejects multi-byte content whose UTF-8 byte length exceeds MAX_INPUT_SIZE while content.length does not.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/bmad/parser.ts plus a BMAD-specific parser regression test.

items.title: Invalid structured BMAD YAML paths are silently dropped from successful parses
items.recommendation: Make bmadToAPS surface conversion diagnostics. At minimum, throw when errors.length > 0 so BMADFormatAdapter.parse returns createParseError; alternatively return a richer internal result and pass warnings/errors through the adapter result.
items.reproduction: Parse an agent YAML document with metadata.id set to '../escape.md' and required metadata/persona fields present. safePath throws, bmadToAPS catches it into errors, then returns an APS plan without the agent change; BMADFormatAdapter.parse reports success.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests are for generic parsing/serialization. Existing BMAD path tests only cover requirement-ID generated paths and do not exercise structured YAML path fields such as agent metadata.id, menu workflow paths, module code, or module directories.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a BMAD adapter test with valid agent YAML except metadata.id: '../escape.md' and assert parse returns success false with an INVALID_PATH error, or returns a warning/error if the chosen contract permits partial parses.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/bmad/parser.ts and packages/adapters/src/bmad/format-adapter.ts parse result plumbing, plus structured-YAML invalid-path tests.

items.title: Warning result consistency check ignores blocking, suppressed, and category totals
items.recommendation: Extend validateWarningResultConsistency to recompute and compare byCategory, suppressed, blocking, and all expected severity buckets. Prefer comparing against createWarningResult(result.warnings).summary so the helper and producer stay aligned.
items.reproduction: Create a WarningResult with one unsuppressed error warning and summary.blocking set to 0, or mutate createWarningResult([errorWarning]).summary.blocking = 0; validateWarningResultConsistency still returns true as long as total and supplied bySeverity entries match.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for the contracts warning helpers, and the discovered validation tests only exercise APS plan validation/createPlan hash handling, not WarningResult consistency.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a WarningResult helper test that mutates each derived summary field (byCategory, bySeverity omission, suppressed, blocking) and expects validateWarningResultConsistency to return false.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/contracts/schemas/warning.schema.ts plus focused tests for warning result consistency

items.title: Failed watcher startup leaves the multi-agent watch lock alive
items.recommendation: Wrap the post-initialize startup sequence in try/catch and cleanup concurrencyContext and the partially-started watcher on any failure before rethrowing. Alternatively set a separate lifecycle state so stop() always cleans up an initialized concurrency context even when start() did not complete.
items.reproduction: Mock createConcurrencyContext with cleanup and lock renewal spies, mock FileWatcher.start to reject, call new WatchOrchestrator(...default multiAgent...).start(), then assert cleanup was not called and stop() still does not call it.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover FileWatcher startup behaviour and git/debouncer helpers, but there is no orchestrator test exercising start failure after multi-agent initialisation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an orchestrator test where multi-agent initialisation succeeds, FileWatcher.start rejects, and the test asserts concurrencyContext.cleanup() is called and a subsequent stop() is harmless.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/watch/orchestrator.ts startup error handling plus an orchestrator regression test.

items.title: Git octal path decoding corrupts non-ASCII filenames
items.recommendation: Prefer `git status --porcelain -z` and parse NUL-delimited raw paths, including rename records, to avoid quote decoding entirely. If keeping quoted parsing, collect octal escapes as bytes and decode them with UTF-8 TextDecoder instead of String.fromCharCode per byte.
items.reproduction: Mock gitExec to return ` M "caf\303\251.md"\n`, then call filterUnstaged([resolve('/repo', 'café.md')]). The parser produces `/repo/cafÃ©.md`, so the input path is filtered out.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The git-status tests cover quoted ASCII paths with spaces and rename arrows, but they do not include octal-escaped multi-byte filenames.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests for getFileStatus, filterUnstaged, and getChangedFiles using mocked porcelain output with UTF-8 octal escapes such as `caf\303\251.md`, asserting the returned path is `café.md` and that filterUnstaged matches the Unicode input path.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/watch/git-status.ts path parsing plus git-status regression tests for non-ASCII filenames.

items.title: Plugin metadata version is stale
items.recommendation: Keep plugin.meta.version in sync with package.json, preferably by generating or importing it from package metadata during build if the project supports that pattern.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included rule tests exercise only individual rules; there is no test for the exported plugin object or its metadata.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an index test that imports the plugin and asserts plugin.meta.name and plugin.meta.version match package.json.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/eslint-plugin-anvil/src/index.ts and add focused coverage for the exported plugin metadata.

items.title: Real-send migration responses can silently include the dry-run discriminator
items.recommendation: Make the send branch reject discriminator drift, for example by adding `dryRun: z.never().optional()` with strict object handling, or by using a stricter object policy/refinement that fails when `dryRun` is present on real-send responses.
items.reproduction: Parse a payload like `{ dryRun: true, source: 'manual', total: 1, sent: 1, failed: 0, results: [] }` with `SendMigrationResponseSchema`; the dry-run branch fails because dry-run-specific fields are absent, then the send branch succeeds after stripping `dryRun`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and there is no evidence of a contract test asserting that real-send responses reject a `dryRun` property.

items.title: Structured debug data bypasses log sanitisation
items.recommendation: Convert non-string data through a bounded serializer or util.inspect, then run sanitizeForLog on the resulting text before logging. Keep depth/length limits to avoid unexpectedly large debug output.

items.title: Explicit undefined default is ignored by parseSeverity
items.recommendation: Remove the default parameter initializer and distinguish omitted arguments from an explicit undefined default, for example by checking arguments.length before assigning the default fallback.

items.title: Backslash path segments are normalised after traversal validation
items.recommendation: Reject both '/' and '\\' traversal separators before platform-specific normalisation, or normalise backslashes to slashes before validating segments. Validate by splitting on '/' and rejecting empty, '.', '..', null-byte, and absolute-prefix cases as required by the intended contract.

items.title: Expired or stale lock takeover can grant the same lock to multiple agents
items.recommendation: Serialize forceAcquire with the same lock-file sentinel used by createLock, then re-read the lock while holding the sentinel and only take over if it is still expired/stale and still represents the holder that was observed before waiting.
items.reproduction: Create an expired lock, then have two LockManager instances with different agent IDs call acquire({ type: 'action', resource: 'gate' }) concurrently. With the current forceAcquire path, both calls can return acquired: true under the read-before-write interleaving.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing expired-lock test exercises a single takeover after expiry; it does not race two takeover attempts against the same expired or stale lock.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that seeds an expired lock and runs two different agents' acquire calls concurrently, asserting exactly one result is acquired and the loser reports the winner as heldBy.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/concurrency/lock-manager.ts plus a concurrent stale/expired takeover test in lock-manager.test.ts

items.title: Queue leave and timeout cleanup bypass the queue file lock
items.recommendation: Route every queue mutation through one locked helper that acquires `${queuePath}.lock`, reloads the current queue, applies the mutation, and writes or unlinks the file before releasing the lock.
items.reproduction: Have agent A and B queued, then run agent A leave while agent C joins the same queue. If leave reads before C's locked write and writes after it, C's entry can disappear from the queue file.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Queue tests cover sequential join, leave, status, and priority behaviour; they do not interleave join with leave or cleanup across QueueManager instances.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a multi-manager race test for join versus leave and another for join versus cleanupTimedOut, asserting no entries are lost and timed-out entries are the only removals.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/concurrency/queue-manager.ts and queue-manager.test.ts

items.title: File cache index updates lose entries across concurrent provider instances
items.recommendation: Protect index read-modify-write operations with a cache index lock, reload the index while holding the lock, apply the mutation, and then save. Avoid using a stale in-memory index across locked mutations unless it is refreshed or versioned.
items.reproduction: Instantiate two FileCacheProvider objects for the same workspace, make both load an empty index, then set different keys concurrently. The final index can contain only one key even though both entry files were written.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The file cache tests cover sequential set/get, persistence, expiration, invalidation, and HMAC checks; they do not exercise concurrent writes from separate provider instances.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that runs Promise.all over two FileCacheProvider instances writing different keys to the same cache directory, then verifies a fresh provider can retrieve both keys and stats entries equals 2.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/cache/providers/file-cache.ts and file-cache.test.ts

items.recommendation: Parse DATABASE_URL with `new URL(databaseUrl)` and disable SSL only when the hostname is exactly `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `::1`. Keep SSL enabled by default for all other hosts.

items.title: Create is not concurrency-safe for per-actor active key uniqueness
items.recommendation: Make the invariant atomic. Prefer a database partial unique index for active actor rows and handle the unique-violation path explicitly, or use a transaction-level advisory lock keyed by actor_email before the SELECT/INSERT. If revoke can affect multiple rows, write one audit row per returned id or enforce uniqueness so that multiple rows cannot be returned.

items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this script, and a single-process happy path test would not exercise the concurrent SELECT/INSERT interleaving.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that starts two concurrent create operations for the same actor with different bearers and asserts that at most one active key exists and the loser exits with the expected database error.
items.minimumFixScope: admin-key create transaction logic plus the admin_keys uniqueness constraint or locking strategy; update revoke audit handling if multiple active duplicates remain possible.

items.title: Documented create output uses hashed_key but script emits hashedKey
items.recommendation: Align the emitted JSON with the documented contract, or update the documented contract and every consumer to use `hashedKey`. For database-facing scripts, matching the snake_case column name in the output is likely the least surprising option.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided to assert the stdout JSON shape for the create action or to exercise the Pulumi consumer contract.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a script-level test for `create` that stubs pg, captures stdout, and asserts the exact JSON keys expected by the Pulumi component.
items.minimumFixScope: Update either the create stdout object or the documented contract and consumer expectations; add a focused stdout-shape regression test.

items.title: Path validation can be bypassed by symlink swaps between check and filesystem operation
items.recommendation: Avoid treating a prevalidated string path as a security boundary when baseDir contents may be mutable by untrusted code. Implement operations using descriptor-relative traversal with no-follow semantics for path components where available, or narrow and document the contract so FileStorage is only used with a trusted, non-concurrently-mutated baseDir. For write/delete, do not perform the final operation through a path that can be reinterpreted after validation.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests create symlinks before invoking FileStorage and assert that resolvePath rejects those stable paths. They do not simulate a path component changing between the resolvePath check and the subsequent fs.readFile/fs.writeFile/fs.unlink operation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that controls the gap between validation and fs.writeFile/fs.unlink, for example by mocking the fs operation to swap an already-validated internal directory or file path to a symlink pointing outside baseDir immediately before delegating to the real filesystem call, then assert the outside target is not read, written, or deleted.
items.minimumFixScope: FileStorage path resolution and filesystem operation implementation; at minimum the security contract for FileStorage must exclude attacker-writable or concurrently mutable base directories.

items.title: Ignored Rego violations are still emitted as warnings
items.recommendation: Have the generic new-violation rule preserve or respect `v.severity`, or exclude ignored/info-level violations from `warn`. If the intent is only summary accounting, keep it out of the `warn` rule path.
items.reproduction: Evaluate the generated policy with an `input.architecture.violations` entry that has `is_new: true` and `severity: "ignore"`; the generic `new-violation` rule still contributes a warning message.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests assert that a new-violation rule and warn rules are generated as text, but they do not evaluate the generated policy with `ignore` or `info` severities.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an OPA evaluation test for generated Rego where a new ignored violation produces no `deny` and no `warn` messages.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust the `new-violation` Rego generation and add semantic policy tests for each supported severity.

items.title: Violation IDs can collide after lossy sanitisation
items.recommendation: Generate IDs from a lossless representation, for example `sha256(JSON.stringify([fromFile, toFile, line]))`, or encode each segment losslessly. Add migration/backwards-compatibility handling for existing baseline IDs if needed.
items.reproduction: Call `createViolationId('src/a-b.ts', 'src/c.ts', 1)` and `createViolationId('src/a_b.ts', 'src/c.ts', 1)`; both return `src_a_b_ts:src_c_ts:1`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover stable IDs and different line/target values, but not two distinct paths that normalise to the same string after replacement.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test asserting two edges that differ only by punctuation such as `a-b.ts` versus `a_b.ts` receive different violation IDs and are classified separately against a baseline.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `createViolationId` and the baseline comparison paths that depend on it; add focused tests for collision resistance.

items.title: Explicit Rego rule generation does not escape layer names
items.recommendation: Use a single helper based on `JSON.stringify` or equivalent Rego string literal escaping for every generated string value, including layer names, rule names used in comments, and severities. Alternatively, validate layer and rule identifiers to a strict safe subset before code generation.
items.reproduction: Use a definition with a layer key such as `bad"layer` and an explicit forbidden rule from that layer; the generated line becomes an invalid `v.from_layer == "bad"layer"` Rego expression.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests only use simple identifier-like layer and rule names and assert substrings; they do not parse the generated Rego or cover escaped characters in YAML layer names.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a generation test with quoted/backslash layer names and verify the resulting Rego parses, or add schema validation tests that reject unsupported identifiers.
items.minimumFixScope: Update explicit rule string interpolation in `rego-generator.ts` and cover generated Rego parsing for non-trivial layer names.

items.title: Template defaults leak mutable nested state across calls
items.recommendation: Deep-clone template defaults before returning them, for example with `structuredClone`, or clone each layer object and its arrays explicitly. Consider freezing the constants in tests to catch accidental mutation.
items.reproduction: Create a starter definition, push a value into `def.layers.lib.depends_on`, then call `createDefinitionFromTemplate('starter')` again. The later definition observes the earlier mutation.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing coverage checks that the top-level return object is not the same reference, but it does not mutate nested layer objects or arrays and then request defaults again.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that mutates `getTemplateDefaults('layered').presentation.depends_on` and asserts a subsequent `getTemplateDefaults('layered')` call returns the original unmodified dependencies.
items.minimumFixScope: Change `getTemplateDefaults` to return fully independent layer definitions and cover `createDefinitionFromTemplate` because it exposes those defaults to callers.

items.title: OpenAPI generation script uses an undeclared runner
items.recommendation: Declare `tsx` in this package's devDependencies, or rewrite the script to use a declared runtime path. Keep the README and script command aligned.
items.reproduction: In a clean install containing only this package's declared dependencies, run `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/anvil-kindling-integration generate:openapi`; the shell cannot resolve `tsx`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked Vitest suite does not execute package lifecycle scripts, and the package has no test that verifies the OpenAPI generator command is runnable from declared dependencies.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a lightweight script smoke check in package validation, or include generate:openapi in the relevant package CI command after adding the missing devDependency.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/kindling-integration/package.json devDependencies and, if needed, the README command.

items.title: Validation helpers return blank errors for field-level schema failures
items.recommendation: Use result.error.issues to build path-aware messages, or return the ZodError/flattened fieldErrors so callers receive actionable validation diagnostics.
items.reproduction: Call validateQueryRequest({ scope: 'session', shape: 'timeline', format: 'json' }) or validateObservation({ kind: 'session_start' }); the parse fails, but the returned error string is empty because only root _errors are joined.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests only assert that invalid inputs are rejected; they do not assert that the returned error payload is non-empty or identifies the failed field.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add assertions that invalid query and observation inputs return an error containing the relevant field path, such as `session_id` or `timestamp`.
items.minimumFixScope: Change validateQueryRequest, validateQueryResponse, and validateObservation error formatting; update affected tests to check diagnostic content.

items.title: Detected sensitive observations can still be persisted unredacted
items.recommendation: Make detection and redaction use the same rule set. Either reject observations whenever a detected sensitive value cannot be redacted, or add redaction rules for every contract-level sensitive pattern and verify the redacted observation no longer triggers validateNoSensitiveData before calling store.emit.
items.reproduction: Emit an action_executed observation with details.command like `tool --api_key=abc123` or `ssh -i ~/.ssh/private_key user@host` through KindlingService using a fake store. The sensitive check is positive, but the stored observation still contains the original sensitive marker/value when it only matched the contract-level detector.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The malicious AI suite asserts that containsSensitiveData detects these cases, but it never exercises KindlingService.emit or redactSensitiveFields to prove the persisted observation is actually scrubbed.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a KindlingService.emit test with an in-memory IKindlingStore that records the emitted observation. Use commands containing `--api_key=abc123` and `~/.ssh/private_key`, then assert the stored JSON no longer contains the original sensitive substrings and either passes validateNoSensitiveData or is rejected.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/kindling-integration/src/sensitive-data-validator.ts and KindlingService.emit; add focused tests in packages/kindling-integration/src/malicious-ai.test.ts or a new service test.

items.title: Warning result consistency validation ignores blocking and suppression summary fields
items.recommendation: Recompute and compare byCategory, suppressed, and blocking inside validateWarningResultConsistency. Also reject missing or extra severity/category counts if those are not intended to be tolerated.
items.reproduction: Construct a WarningResult with one unsuppressed severity 'error' warning, summary.total = 1, summary.bySeverity.error = 1, but summary.blocking = 0. validateWarningResultConsistency returns true even though createWarningResult would produce blocking = 1.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The provided tests cover APS and feature flag schemas only; no linked test exercises warning summary consistency or malformed WarningResult summaries.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add warning schema tests that alter blocking, suppressed, and byCategory in a createWarningResult output and assert validateWarningResultConsistency returns false for each mismatch.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/contracts/src/schemas/warning.schema.ts plus a focused warning schema test file or existing contracts schema test coverage.

items.title: Feature flag targeting rules can reference missing variants
items.recommendation: Extend FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema.check to collect variant keys and reject every targeting rule whose variant is not present in variants, with the issue path pointing at targeting[i].variant.
items.reproduction: Validate a flag with variants enabled/disabled and targeting: [{ conditions: [{ attribute: 'environment', operator: 'equals', value: 'prod' }], variant: 'typo' }]. FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema.safeParse currently succeeds.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked feature flag tests verify valid targeting rules, empty rule fields, and defaultVariant validation, but they never exercise a targeting rule that references a non-existent variant.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema test that uses validFlag({ targeting: [{ conditions: [{ attribute: 'environment', operator: 'equals', value: 'prod' }], variant: 'missing' }] }) and expects safeParse(...).success to be false.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/contracts/src/schemas/feature-flags.schema.ts plus the associated feature-flags schema test.

items.title: Pool cap behaviour is not covered by the library test
items.recommendation: Add a regression test that validates the cap in an isolated process before any other rayon consumer can initialise the global pool. If direct global-pool testing is too fragile for unit tests, factor the cap calculation into a small pure helper and test that helper, then add one integration or subprocess smoke test for `init_global` applying it first.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The sole included test only calls `init_global()` twice and asserts no panic by implication; its own comment states that it does not assert the resulting thread count.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Run a subprocess or dedicated integration binary that calls `eddacraft_anvil_rayon_init::init_global()` before any `par_iter`, then asserts `rayon::current_num_threads() == (num_cpus::get() / 2).max(1)`.
items.minimumFixScope: Add focused coverage for the cap calculation and first-initialisation behaviour in `crates/anvil-rayon-init`.

items.title: Non-recursive loading silently overwrites duplicate module IDs
items.recommendation: Move the duplicate-ID check before the recursive/non-recursive split, or add the same modules.has guard to the non-recursive branch before modules.set.
items.reproduction: Load an index containing two module headings with the same ID using loadPlan(path, { recursive: false }); the returned modules Map contains only the later entry for that ID.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The recursive=false test only verifies that a normal index skips loading task content; it does not cover duplicate module IDs in that mode.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a duplicate-module index fixture and assert loadPlan(fixture, { recursive: false }) rejects with ParseError matching duplicate module ID.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/aps/src/loader/index.ts duplicate guard placement plus one loader regression test.

items.title: Top-level leaf specs with “Modules …” headings are routed through the index loader
items.recommendation: Apply the same real-index probe at the root before calling loadMultiModulePlan, or make detectIndexFile only recognise actual index module sections and require parsed modules before selecting the multi-module loader.
items.reproduction: Create a valid single-file APS leaf document with an H1, valid task content, and an H2 named "Modules impacted". loadPlan(path) will take the index branch at packages/aps/src/loader/index.ts:91 instead of loadSingleFilePlan.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing false-positive test loads an index whose child module contains "Modules impacted", so it exercises the nested fallback path only. There is no root-level single-file false-positive test.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a temporary or fixture single-file APS leaf with "## Modules impacted" and assert loadPlan returns isMultiModule=false with the expected module and tasks.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/aps/src/loader/index.ts root index detection plus one loader regression test.

items.title: Index module path placeholders produce ambiguous Markdown links
items.recommendation: Change path examples to avoid nested square brackets inside link syntax, for example `[./modules/module-name.aps.md](./modules/module-name.aps.md)` or `[module-name](./modules/module-name.aps.md)`, consistently across minimal, standard, and full index templates.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked test checks only that some Markdown link-looking text exists and does not validate rendered/parsed Markdown or assert the exact placeholder-safe form.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Assert that generated index templates do not contain bracketed placeholders inside Markdown link labels or destinations, or parse them with the same Markdown parser used by APS and verify the expected link URL/text.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the index template path lines in all variants and tighten the index path-link test.

items.title: Trace file creation can follow a raced symlink before validation
items.recommendation: Open trace files with no-follow semantics on Unix, for example OpenOptionsExt::custom_flags(libc::O_NOFOLLOW) plus create_new(true) for the absent-file path or an openat-style flow. Keep the post-open inode check, but make the open itself refuse symlinks.
items.reproduction: On Unix, set ANVIL_TRACE_SINK=file=<path in attacker-writable directory>. Race creation of <path> as a symlink after validate_existing_trace_file observes NotFound but before OpenOptions::open runs. The function can open the symlink target before returning TraceSink.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included Unix tests cover existing non-regular paths and private regular files, but they do not exercise the missing-path creation case or a symlink substitution race.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Unix test for a missing path where the final path is a symlink at open time, and assert open_trace_file returns an error without creating or opening the symlink target. If deterministic race injection is hard, factor the open path to make the NotFound-to-open transition testable.
items.minimumFixScope: crates/anvil-observability/src/lib.rs open_trace_file Unix opening flags and corresponding Unix tests.

items.title: Published CLI reports a different version than the package
items.recommendation: Read the version from package metadata during build/runtime, inject it via a build constant, or keep a single source of truth so the CLI version tracks `tools/codemods/package.json`.
items.reproduction: Build the package and run `node tools/codemods/dist/cli.js --version`; it reports `0.0.1` while the package version is `0.3.0-beta`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this package, and the feature metadata lists an empty tests array.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CLI test that invokes `--version` and compares the output with `tools/codemods/package.json` version.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `tools/codemods/src/cli.ts` version wiring or package build metadata so the Commander version matches `tools/codemods/package.json`.

items.title: Split imports drop aliases and type-only import qualifiers
items.recommendation: Preserve the full named import structure when grouping symbols: include `name`, `alias`, and type-only metadata from ts-morph, and set `isTypeOnly` on inserted import declarations when appropriate. Add explicit handling for mixed type/value imports if the AST API requires separate declarations.
items.reproduction: Apply the codemod to `import type { APSPlan as Plan, GateRunner } from '@eddacraft/anvil-core';` or `import { APSPlanSchema as Schema, GateRunner } from '@eddacraft/anvil-core';`. The recreated imports contain bare symbol names and no import kind preservation, so existing `Plan` or `Schema` references are no longer imported as written.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this package, and the feature metadata lists an empty tests array.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests for split imports containing aliases, `import type`, and `type` named specifiers, asserting the transformed source preserves aliases and type-only semantics.
items.minimumFixScope: Change `processSplitImports` in `tools/codemods/src/transforms/rewrite-imports.ts` to group structured import specifier data instead of bare strings.

items.title: Bare core imports are counted and reported twice
items.recommendation: Handle bare `@eddacraft/anvil-core` imports in one place. Prefer running split-import logic before simple path rewrites, or make `processImportDeclaration` skip the bare core package when named imports are present so symbol-based splitting owns that case.
items.reproduction: Run the codemod against a file containing `import { APSPlanSchema, GateRunner, OPAExecutor } from '@eddacraft/anvil-core';`. Dry-run output includes the simple contracts rewrite plus split entries; applying the codemod rewrites the whole import to `@eddacraft/anvil-contracts` instead of splitting runtime and policy symbols.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this package, and the feature metadata lists an empty tests array.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a vitest covering a mixed bare core import and assert dry-run returns only the package-specific split changes and apply mode emits separate imports for contracts, runtime, and policy symbols.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `tools/codemods/src/transforms/rewrite-imports.ts` so bare core imports cannot be processed by both rewrite paths.

items.title: Public declarations expose Buffer without publishing Node type support
items.recommendation: Either avoid the Node-global type in the public contract, for example by using Uint8Array or importing a type from node:buffer with the required type package declared, or add @types/node to the package's published dependency surface so consumers receive the declaration dependency automatically.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests exercise the package as an installed dependency from a consumer project without the repository root devDependencies. The local typecheck uses workspace-level Node typings, masking the missing manifest contract.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a declaration-consumer fixture that installs or links only @eddacraft/anvil-ports and runs tsc without root workspace devDependencies, asserting that importing IStorageProvider typechecks.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/anvil/ports/package.json and, if choosing to avoid Node globals, packages/anvil/ports/src/interfaces/storage.interface.ts.

items.title: weightedConfidence can produce out-of-range EmberConfidence values
items.recommendation: Constrain weights to positive or at least non-negative values, either by parsing with a small Zod schema or by throwing when any weight is negative. Also validate or clamp the final result before returning an EmberConfidence.
items.reproduction: weightedConfidence([{ score: 1 as EmberConfidence, weight: 2 }, { score: 0 as EmberConfidence, weight: -1 }]) returns 2 cast as EmberConfidence.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test only covers positive weights and the zero-length case indirectly through other utilities. It does not cover negative weights or verify the result still satisfies EmberConfidenceSchema.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that negative weights are rejected, and another that EmberConfidenceSchema.safeParse(weightedConfidence(validPositiveWeights)).success remains true.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/contracts/confidence.ts and confidence utility tests.

items.title: MemoryObjectExtended is not compatible with the EDDA-001 memory schema it claims to extend
items.recommendation: Define MemoryObjectExtended in terms of the base type, for example by importing type MemoryObject and using interface MemoryObjectExtended extends MemoryObject for additive fields. If the attribution shape intentionally changed, model it as a named migration or Omit<MemoryObject, 'attribution'> with clear schemas/tests rather than labelling it as core EDDA-001.
items.reproduction: Parse a valid EDDA-001 memory with MemoryObjectSchema, then try to add scope/authority/enforcement/review_policy and use it as MemoryObjectExtended. TypeScript rejects the attribution shape and required optional fields; at runtime, a MemoryObjectExtended-shaped attribution fails MemoryObjectSchema parsing.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise MemoryObjectSchema and related typed memory schemas, but there are no tests for edda-extended.ts or assignability/parse compatibility between MemoryObject and MemoryObjectExtended.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a type-level test or tsd-style fixture showing that a MemoryObject plus extension fields satisfies MemoryObjectExtended, and a runtime test that the shared core fields still parse through MemoryObjectSchema.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/contracts/edda-extended.ts and a focused compatibility test.

items.title: buildEvolutionGraph can return dangling evolution links
items.recommendation: Make buildEvolutionGraph enforce referential integrity. Either reject missing endpoints during graph construction, include placeholder nodes with an explicit partial/incomplete marker, or skip out-of-set links when building a graph for a partial memory set. Keep EvolutionGraphSchema or a refinement aligned with that choice.
items.reproduction: Call buildEvolutionGraph with one parsed memory whose evolution.superseded_by is another valid MemoryId not included in the memories array. The returned graph contains one node and one link to a missing new_memory_id; validateEvolutionGraph(graph).valid is false, and findLatestMemory(graph) returns null.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: evolution.test.ts builds graphs where both sides of every supersedes/superseded_by relationship are present. It does not cover partial memory sets or missing link endpoints.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that builds a graph from a memory whose superseded_by target is absent and asserts the chosen contract: buildEvolutionGraph throws, omits the dangling link, or creates a validated placeholder node. Also assert findLatestMemory does not silently return null for a one-node partial graph.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/contracts/evolution.ts plus evolution graph tests.

items.title: mergeProvenanceChains can return an invalid ProvenanceChain for empty input
items.recommendation: Reject empty input with a clear error, change the signature to require a non-empty tuple, or return null/undefined for empty aggregation. Also parse or otherwise assert the returned object against ProvenanceChainSchema before returning.
items.reproduction: ProvenanceChainSchema.safeParse(mergeProvenanceChains([])).success evaluates to false because kindling_sources is empty.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The mergeProvenanceChains tests only pass one or more non-empty chains. They do not assert behaviour for an empty merge request.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a mergeProvenanceChains([]) test that asserts the selected contract, preferably that the function throws a clear error instead of returning a schema-invalid ProvenanceChain.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/contracts/provenance.ts and provenance tests.

items.title: Mandatory plan, gate, and action IDs accept empty strings
items.recommendation: Use z.string().min(1) at minimum for plan_id, gate_eval_id, and action_id, and preferably encode the expected ID formats where they are known.
items.reproduction: PlanQuerySchema.safeParse({ scope: 'plan', plan_id: '', shape: 'entity' }) succeeds; the same applies to gate_eval_id and action_id with empty strings.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests reject missing IDs, but they do not cover empty-string IDs for plan, gate, or action queries.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests asserting PlanQuerySchema, GateQuerySchema, and ActionQuerySchema reject empty-string identifiers.
items.minimumFixScope: query-contract.ts schema refinements plus malicious-ai.test.ts coverage for empty identifiers.

items.title: Sensitive observations can still be persisted unredacted
items.recommendation: Make sensitive handling fail closed: either reject observations when any detected issue cannot be redacted, or add redaction coverage for every containsSensitiveData class and verify the post-redaction payload no longer triggers detection. Also route AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit through the same validation/redaction path or mark/drop sensitive content before appendObservation.
items.reproduction: Use an enabled KindlingService with a mock store and emit an action_executed observation whose details.command is `ssh -i ~/.ssh/private_key user@host`; containsSensitiveData reports sensitive, but redactSensitiveFields has no private-key-path replacement, so the mock store receives the original command. Calling AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit with the same observation serializes it directly into content.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests assert containsSensitiveData detects sensitive payloads, but they do not exercise redactSensitiveFields, KindlingService.emit with a capturing store, or AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit output.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that emit the existing private_key and token-in-error fixtures through KindlingService.emit and AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit, then assert the persisted content no longer contains the original sensitive substrings or that emission rejects the observation.
items.minimumFixScope: sensitive-data-validator.ts plus KindlingService/adapter emission paths; add focused tests in malicious-ai.test.ts or a service-specific test.

items.title: Post-query limit enforcement ignores the caller's smaller per-query limits
items.recommendation: Carry the effective request limits into post-query enforcement. For each query method, compute effective limits as min(requested limit, config limit) and pass those limits to enforceQueryLimits for that response. Consider also applying response limits inside KindlingService.query for callers that use the lower-level service directly.
items.reproduction: Use a KindlingQueryService whose underlying service has config.query_limits.max_results = 100 and whose query method returns 50 observations regardless of request. Calling querySession(validUuid, { max_results: 10 }) returns all 50 because applyLimits enforces 100, not 10.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests validate schema maximums and manually validate truncation metadata, but they do not use KindlingQueryService with a store/service that returns more rows than the request asked for.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a KindlingQueryService test with a mock service returning more observations than options.max_results and assert the returned response is truncated to the requested count with truncation metadata set.
items.minimumFixScope: query-service.ts limit application, with a focused query service regression test.

items.title: Adapter claims APS export support while serialize always fails
items.recommendation: Implement APS markdown serialization, or override canExport to return false for APS formats until serialization is available and update the tests to match that contract.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The test suite asserts canExport but never calls serialize for APS markdown, so the advertised capability is not exercised end to end.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that builds a minimal valid APSPlan, asserts canExport('aps') is true only when serialize returns success, and verifies the emitted markdown can be parsed back or at least contains the expected APS task fields.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/aps-markdown/adapter.ts and packages/adapters/src/aps-markdown/__tests__/adapter.test.ts.

items.title: Detected APS index files parse into empty plans instead of preserving modules
items.recommendation: Either add an index parsing branch that preserves module links in the APSPlan representation, or stop detecting index files as parseable until index conversion is implemented. If index import is intentionally unsupported, return a parse error instead of an empty successful plan.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover index detection only; all parse tests use leaf specs or inline task documents.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that passes the existing Modules-section fixture through detect and parse, then asserts either a structured module representation is preserved or parse fails with an explicit unsupported-index error.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/aps-markdown/adapter.ts parse/conversion logic plus aps-markdown adapter tests.

items.title: File cache index overwrites concurrent provider updates
items.recommendation: Serialize index mutations across providers/processes or reload and merge the latest index before saving. A lock file around load-modify-save, append-only entry discovery, or compare-and-retry write protocol would avoid lost updates.
items.reproduction: Create two FileCacheProvider instances pointing at the same temp directory. Let both load the index before either save completes, then set different keys concurrently with Promise.all. Re-open a third provider and only one key may be present in index.json, depending on the final save order.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The file-cache tests use one provider instance for normal set/get paths and only create a second provider after the first set has completed for persistence. They do not exercise concurrent writers sharing one cache directory.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test with two FileCacheProvider instances sharing one temp cache directory that concurrently set distinct keys, then verify a fresh provider can read both entries and stats/index entry count is 2.
items.minimumFixScope: Change FileCacheProvider index update/save logic to coordinate or merge concurrent mutations, and add multi-provider concurrency coverage.

items.title: All-gate invalidation pattern does not match real gate cache keys
items.recommendation: Change allGateInvalidationPattern() to return 'gate:**', or change provider wildcard semantics so 'gate:*' intentionally matches all remaining segments. Keep the helper and provider semantics aligned in tests.
items.reproduction: Set a cache entry under key 'gate:check:eslint:abc', then call invalidatePattern(allGateInvalidationPattern()). The pattern is 'gate:*', so patternToRegex builds /^gate:[^:]*$/ and the entry is not invalidated.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: cache-key.test.ts only asserts that allGateInvalidationPattern() returns the literal string 'gate:*'. Provider tests verify literal patterns directly, but no test passes allGateInvalidationPattern() to a provider with real generated gate keys.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a cache provider test that stores 'gate:check:eslint:abc', calls invalidatePattern(allGateInvalidationPattern()), and expects the entry count invalidated to be 1 for both memory and file providers.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the all-gate invalidation helper and its tests; add provider-level coverage for the exported helper.

items.title: README omits current device-confirm auth and public-key requirements
items.recommendation: Update the endpoint table to mark /auth/device/confirm as licence-authenticated, and add LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY plus LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY_KID, if operator-managed, to the environment variable table with the expected SPKI/KID contract.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests verify the implemented auth and key behaviour, but no documentation drift test checks that README endpoint auth and environment-variable tables match the route and health contracts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a lightweight docs contract check that asserts documented required env vars include LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY and that the README auth table marks /api/v1/auth/device/confirm consistently with the route's requireAuth middleware.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/README.md endpoint and environment-variable sections, plus optional docs-contract coverage.

items.title: Published package omits its own operational scripts
items.recommendation: Either include the operational assets in package.json files, or remove package-level scripts that are only valid from the monorepo checkout. If the migration runner is supported from the package, ship scripts plus the SQL migration directory, or copy SQL assets into dist and update the runner path.
items.reproduction: Pack the package and inspect the tarball contents; package.json remains, but scripts/migrate.mjs, scripts/check-runtime-cjs.cjs, and src/db/migrations/*.sql are absent.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests exercise migration logic from source fixtures, but there is no package contract test that packs @eddacraft/anvil-api and runs or verifies the advertised package scripts from the packed file set.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package smoke test that runs pnpm pack --dry-run --json for apps/anvil-api and asserts the tarball file list contains the migration runner, runtime CJS checker, and SQL migration assets required by the package scripts.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/package.json files allow-list and, if needed, the build/migration asset-copy path plus a package pack-content regression test.

items.title: Token consume queries can win stale validity races
items.recommendation: Move validity predicates into the atomic consume statements. Refresh-token consume should require consumed_at IS NULL, revoked_at IS NULL, and expires_at > now(); device-code consume should require confirmed_at IS NOT NULL and expires_at > now(). If callers need different response shapes, return a small result enum rather than relying on stale pre-checks.
items.reproduction: Session refresh race: request A reads an unrevoked refresh token, then an admin revoke transaction sets revoked_at before A calls consumeRefreshToken. A's UPDATE still matches because it only checks consumed_at, then A inserts a new refresh token and signs a licence.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Route tests mock consumeRefreshToken and consumeDeviceCode, so they verify caller branching but not the SQL predicates. apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__/queries.test.ts covers scope lookup and revoke-family transaction behaviour only; it has no assertions for the consume SQL.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add query-level tests with a recording tagged-template mock that assert consumeRefreshToken and consumeDeviceCode include the revoked/expiry validity predicates and return false/null when no row is consumed.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/db/queries.ts consume predicates, plus any route handling adjustments for newly failed consume attempts.

items.title: Dry-run migrations create the tracking table
items.recommendation: Make dry-run read-only. For dry runs, inspect the tracking table only if it already exists, treat a missing tracking table as zero applied migrations, and defer ensureTrackingTable to non-dry-run execution.
items.reproduction: Call runMigrations(runner, { dir, dryRun: true }) with a real database that has no _migrations table; the dry run creates _migrations before listing pending files.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The dry-run test only asserts BEGIN and COMMIT are absent. It does not assert CREATE TABLE is absent, and the fake runner accepts the tracking-table DDL during dry-run.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend the dry-run test to assert no CREATE TABLE call is recorded, and add a missing-tracking-table dry-run case that reports all files pending without creating _migrations.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/db/migrate.ts dry-run control flow and apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__/migrate.test.ts coverage.

items.recommendation: Reject arrays before normalising: if Array.isArray(elements), return the original spec or fail validation explicitly. Keep the visible injection limited to plain record-like element maps.
